title: Heliciton-Assisted Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity from Helical Dirac Current
abstract: We develop a quantized chiral-field mechanism for chirality-induced spin selectivity (CISS). The corresponding quantum is a heliciton: a helical mode with phase coordinate $φ-qz$, screw momentum $\hbar q$, and energy $\hbarΩ_q$. A helical electron can absorb or emit this quantum, converting the static chiral vertex developed in our preceding work into an inelastic resonant scattering process. Using first Born scattering theory, we show that an incident two-spin-channel state generates two heliciton-assisted sidebands. Absorption converts the $\uparrow k$ channel into the $\downarrow,k+q$ sideband, while emission converts the $\downarrow k$ channel into the $\uparrow,k-q$ sideband. Thus the heliciton supplies both the screw momentum and energy needed to turn the handedness-conversion into a resonant spin-selective channel.   The two sidebands inherit the same sampled-current overlap $J_χ(k)$ from the static theory, but acquire different kinematic weights and different resonance detunings. The sideband sector reaches full spin polarization at the respective isolated heliciton resonances, with $P_{\rm sb}(k,q)\simeq +1$ for $Δ_-(k,q)=0$ and $P_{\rm sb}(k,q)\simeq -1$ for $Δ_+(k,q)=0$. Reversing the screw handedness, $q\rightarrow -q$, interchanges the two sideband channels and reverses the polarization. No ad hoc spin-dependent potential is introduced. The spin selectivity comes from three ingredients: helical Dirac-current texture, quantized screw-symmetric environmental motion, and resonant exchange of screw momentum and energy. This identifies CISS as a heliciton-assisted resonance mechanism that produces spin polarization in the inelastic sideband sector.
summary: The paper proposes that Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) can be understood as a resonant inelastic scattering process mediated by a quantized environmental excitation called a 'heliciton.' By coupling the electron to this heliciton, the static chiral potential gains access to energy and momentum exchange channels. This mechanism predicts full spin polarization in sidebands when specific resonance conditions are met, providing a robust theoretical framework for spintronics.
main_problem: To develop a mechanism for Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity (CISS) that incorporates energy exchange with the environment, moving beyond static chiral potentials.
main_result: The heliciton supplies both the necessary screw momentum and energy to convert the static handedness-conversion into a resonant, spin-selective inelastic scattering channel.
method: First Born scattering theory is used on an electron coupled to a quantized environmental mode (heliciton), analyzing resulting sidebands.
model_or_system: A confined Dirac electron interacting with a chiral potential ($\hat{V}_\chi$) whose quantization yields a 'heliciton' quantum. The system dynamics are governed by time-dependent and stationary eigenvalue equations involving the heliciton reservoir energy.
key_observables: Sideband polarization ($P_{sb}$), which reaches full spin polarization at specific resonance detunings ($\Delta_\pm = 0$).
important_parameters: Helhelicon frequency ($\Omega_q$), momentum transfer ($q$), and the linewidth ($\Gamma_q$) of the resonant sidebands.
main_assumptions: The mechanism relies on three ingredients: helical Dirac-current texture, quantized screw-symmetric environmental motion (heliciton), and resonant exchange of energy/momentum. No ad hoc spin-dependent potential is introduced.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the limitation of static potentials to introducing the heliciton quantization, applying first Born scattering theory to derive sideband polarization formulas, and finally confirming that the resonance mechanism provides the necessary spin selectivity signature upon reversing chirality ($q 	o -q$).
why_interesting: This work models a quantum transport phenomenon (CISS) using concepts from open quantum systems—specifically, coupling to an environmental bosonic mode (the heliciton)—which is highly relevant for understanding energy-dependent spin filtering in condensed matter.

Spintronics.note: The paper provides a detailed theoretical framework for achieving spin polarization via resonant inelastic scattering in a confined Dirac electron system, which is highly relevant to quantum-optical descriptions of spin transport.
